headline: Aday Mara recorded 10 points (5-of-6 FGs), three rebounds and three blocks in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: While Mara has started four of Oklahoma City’s last six games, the 21 minutes he logged on Friday were the least he’s played in any of those starts. There were some positives to the rookie’s performance, specifically the field-goal percentage and blocked shots. However, Mara hasn’t done enough with Chet Holmgren (knee) out to become a player who has to be rostered in 12-team leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
body: McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
body: After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
body: After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers.
body: After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Darius Acuff scores 17 points (6-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals, and three 3-pointers in 120-107 loss to the Blazers.
body: Acuff got going in the second half after a bad start. He adjusted to how Portland was guarding him and he started hitting more of his shots. He helped spearhead the comeback late in the fourth after being down 20. He’s getting better each game and is still being one of the best scorers in the NBA this season.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell and Victor Wembanyama will start Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: After a two-game absence, Vassell is available for Friday’s game. His return means that Julian Champagnie will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson Julian Champagnie

headline: The Warriors will start Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, De’Anthony Melton, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Draymond Green against the Spurs on Friday.
body: Steph Curry suffered a right oblique abdominal tear and will be out for tonight’s game. The Warriors made two changes to the starting lineup, first with sliding Draymond Green to the five and replacing Al Horford with Will Richard, and then De’Anthony Melton will start in place of Steph Curry. Richard isn’t a great fantasy player, but Melton is the guy to add if he’s available in your fantasy league.
author: Brian Taylor De'Anthony Melton Will Richard

headline: Devin Vassell (groin) is available for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Vassell is set to return after missing the last two games with a groin injury. Julian Champagnie will likely head back to the bench with De’Aaron Fox (hip) also available.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Charles Bassey (toe) will play against the Spurs on Friday.
body: Bassey was probable prior to this game but will give it a go. He’s a backup center that you can use as a streamer in deeper leagues if you want, or if you really need rebounds in twelve teamers. He’s been helping the Warriors win games which is good to see.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: De’Aaron Fox (hip) is available for Friday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Initially questionable for Friday’s game, Fox is now good to go. He’ll occupy his usual place in the Spurs’ starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Okogie, Ace Bailey, and Jaxson Hayes against the Rockets on Friday.
body: The Jazz will start Josh Okogie over Josh Green in this game. Neither of them are fantasy relevant it shouldn’t impact things very much.
author: Brian Taylor Josh Okogie Josh Green

headline: The Memphis Grizzlies will start Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer, and Isaiah Stewart on Friday against the Pelicans.
body: Zach Edey is out due to injury management, so Isaiah Stewart will get the start against the Pelicans. Stewart could be used as a stream in redraft leagues, especially since Quinten Post is already out, so Stewart is projected to get plenty of minutes.
author: Brian Taylor Isaiah Stewart

headline: The Pelicans will start Jeremiah Fears, Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey, Zion Williamson, and DeAndre Jordan on Friday against the Grizzlies.
body: There have been two changes to the starting lineup from the past game against the Nets. Saddiq Bey is starting in place of Dejounte Murray who is reportedly not playing for the Pelicans again, and DeAndre Jordan will replace Karlo Matković in the starting lineup.
author: Brian Taylor DeAndre Jordan Karlo Matković Saddiq Bey

headline: James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Jaylon Tyson, Peyton Watson and Jarrett Allen will start Friday’s game against the Heat.
body: The Cavaliers are without Evan Mobley, who is sidelined with a toe injury. As a result, Cleveland will go with a smaller lineup, with Tyson filling the void. The other four starters are unchanged.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Miami Heat will start Davion Mitchell, Tim Hardaway Jr., Myron Gardner, Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Bam Adebayo on Friday against the Cavaliers.
body: Pelle Larsson and Klay Thompson are out tonight with injury, so Tim Hardaway Jr. has entered the starting lineup. Myron Gardner gets his first start of the season with Andrew Wiggins remaining on the bench. Gardner has played 20 minutes this season with half of those minutes being played last game against the Jazz.
author: Brian Taylor Andrew Wiggins Tim Hardaway Jr. Myron Gardner

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is out for Saturday’s game against the Heat.
body: Joe’s absence has freed up additional minutes for fellow reserves Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green. That should remain the case on Saturday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tarik Biberović (heel) is out for Saturday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Biberović’s continued absence will not affect fantasy basketball, and he has yet to make his NBA debut.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Morez Johnson Jr. (shin) is probable for Saturday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Johnson played 13 minutes off the bench in Thursday’s loss to the Timberwolves. If available on Saturday, the rookie will likely take on a similar role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Christie (ankle) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Christie is back on the injury report, this time due to a sprained left ankle. After beginning the season as a starter, he’s played limited minutes over the last five games. Caleb Martin has started Dallas’ last four games and should retain that role, regardless of what happens with Christie.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Trail Blazers.
body: Achiuwa is dealing with left ankle soreness that will keep him sidelined for at least one game. With Achiuwa on the sideline, Keegan Murray could rejoin the starting five for the first time since returning from injury.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: The NY Post’s Brian Lewis reports that Nolan Traoré (calf) practiced Friday and will be re-evaluated following practice.
body: Traoré sat out Wednesday’s blowout win over the Pelicans, but Brooklyn went big, starting Danny Wolf, Day’Ron Sharpe, Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. alongside the lone guard, Egor Dëmin. If Traoré is cleared to play Saturday against Memphis, he could rejoin the starting five, with Wolf or Sharpe likely to shift back to the bench.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: The NY Post’s Brian Lewis reports that Mikel Brown Jr. (illness) was not at Friday’s practice.
body: Brown Jr. sat out Sunday against the Mavericks due to a back issue, and he missed Wednesday’s tilt with New Orleans due to the illness. His illness could keep him sidelined for another game, but fantasy managers will need to check his status ahead of Saturday’s matchup with the Grizzlies. Keon Ellis could handle additional minutes if Brown Jr. is forced to miss a third straight game.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reports that Austin Reaves is listed as day-to-day with a bruised heel.
body: According to head coach JJ Redick, Reaves and the Lakers medical staff opted against imaging. This latest update is favorable for the severity of the injury, and Reaves could miss little time, if any at all. If Reaves is forced to sit out, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes could pick up the slack.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is out for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: McGowens’ availability isn’t super impactful to the Pelicans’ rotation, but his absence could free up some extra minutes for Bennedict Mathurin.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bennedict Mathurin (thumb) has been upgraded to questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: With a number of key players sidelined, Mathurin could be in line for additional run against Memphis. He’s averaging just 6.0 points across 15.8 minutes this season, but he’s worth a dart throw on Friday night for fantasy managers in need of his stat set.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, Dejounte Murray (ankle) has requested a trade and is out for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: Murray was previously listed as doubtful due to a left ankle sprain, but this recent update from Charania means that Murray’s status may actually be related to his trade request. The former Hawk and Spur will likely have interest around the league, and his landing spot will dictate his rest-of-season fantasy value. Murray isn’t expected to play for New Orleans again, which means Jeremiah Fears’ stock is way up.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Collin Gillespie provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers on Thursday against the Hornets.
body: Though Gillespie has played well, he hasn’t been as impactful so far this season due to his role being limited. This was his fourth game scoring in double figures this season and his second straight. If he were to see his role expand for any reason, Gillespie would become a must-roster player. For now, he’s just worth keeping an eye on.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (12-of-20 FGs), one rebound, seven assists, three steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 101-96 win over the Hornets on Thursday.
body: After scoring just 17 points in Tuesday’s win, which was a game he only played 29 minutes due to the lopsided score, Booker was able to get back on track in this one. He matched his season high for both steals and three-pointers in the win while also scoring at least 30 points for the fifth time this season. He has been excellent this season and will look to stay hot against the Lakers on Sunday to wrap up the week.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Collin Gillespie provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (5-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers on Tuesday against the Hornets.
body: Though Gillespie has played well, he hasn’t been as impactful so far this season due to his role being limited. This was his fourth game scoring in double figures this season and his second straight. If he were to see his role expand for any reason, Gillespie would become a must-roster player. For now, he’s just worth keeping an eye on.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (12-of-20 FGs), one rebound, seven assists, three steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 101-96 win over the Hornets on Tuesday.
body: After scoring just 17 points in Tuesday’s win, which was a game he only played 29 minutes due to the lopsided score, Booker was able to get back on track in this one. He matched his season high for both steals and three-pointers in the win while also scoring at least 30 points for the fifth time this season. He has been excellent this season and will look to stay hot against the Lakers on Sunday to wrap up the week.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Coby White led the Hornets with 21 points (8-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in a 101-96 loss to the Suns on Thursday.
body: It has taken White some time to get going after missing the start of the year, and he’s still on a minutes restriction, but he was able to have his highest scoring performance of the season in this game. Despite playing less than 20 minutes, White led Charlotte in scoring in what was his best game of the season. Hopefully his role will increase as the season progresses, but he is already starting to tick up his production.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Grant Williams made his season debut on Thursday and contributed 11 points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns.
body: Suiting up for the first time this season after missing the start of the year with a hamstring strain, Williams was able to make an impact immediately. Despite playing just 16 minutes, Williams was able to space the floor and score in double figures. They also outscored the Suns by 11 points when he was on the floor, which was the best mark on the team by far. Williams isn’t a standard-league option, but he is a solid depth piece for Charlotte.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Christian Anderson Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 13 points (4-of-9 FGs), two assists and three three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
body: It has been a rough start to Anderson’s career, but he was able to get some offense going in this one. He set a new career high for scoring, and he has knocked down three triples in two straight games. One of the best shooters in the draft, it is good to see Anderson start to get things going on offense. He isn’t worth rostering in redraft leagues, but he is worth stashing in dynasty formats.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Bones Hyland led the Timberwolves with 24 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, two steals and five three-pointers in a 133-94 win over the Mavericks on Thursday.
body: Hyland had his best game of the season in what ended up being a blowout win for Minnesota. He set season highs for both points and three-pointers while matching his season high for assists. Hyland has been a solid reserve for the Wolves this season, though the production hasn’t come consistently. Despite a fantastic performance, he isn’t worth adding in most formats due to a limited role.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: LaMelo Ball lit up the Mavericks with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, nine assists, two steals and six three-pointers on Thursday.
body: It wasn’t a monster game for LaMelo, but it didn’t need to be. He made the most of his 25 minutes on the court in the blowout win. This was his fifth straight game with at least 20 points, and he set a new season high for assists. LaMelo took some time to get going, but he is starting to get into a groove with Anthony Edwards sidelined. Minnesota has now won five straight games and will look to extend their streak with the Bulls coming to town on Saturday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 22 points (9-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Risacher was the leading scorer for Dallas in this game, though most of his work came after the result had been decided. Risacher had a strong start to the season, specifically on the defensive end. However, he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, though this was a nice outing for him. However, in the month of November, he has only scored in double figures in the games that were decided by at least 35 points, making him a difficult player to trust in fantasy basketball.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: P.J. Washington finished with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds and one three-pointer against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Washington got off to a hot start to this game, scoring 10 points in the first quarter. Unfortunately, foul trouble limited him to just 16 minutes, and he didn’t score over the final three quarters. That pretty much sums this game up for Dallas, as they were outscored by 31 points after the first quarter. They were completely dominated in this game, though Washington was able to start off well, so that is something, I suppose. They’ll look to bounce back in Cleveland on Saturday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.
body: A big fourth quarter led to Trae setting a new season high for scoring. In fact, this was his first 30-point, 10-assist game as a Wizard and the 92nd of his career, which ranks fifth in NBA history. Unfortunately, after scoring his 33rd point at the buzzer with an incredible three-pointer to force overtime, he shot 0-of-7 from the floor in overtime, with the four extra points coming at the free throw line. Still, it was an excellent night for him and was certainly his best performance as a Wizard. It is also worth noting that AJ Dybantsa, despite a rough night, hit a tough mid-range shot to force the second overtime, which was a fun moment for the rookie.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Chris Youngblood (foot) has been ruled out against the Kings on Friday.
body: Youngblood will miss a second straight game, which should allow Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson to take on a few extra minutes. However, neither should see a dramatic boost in production from Youngblood’s absence. Cissoko is already starting and had 19 points on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cam Christie (ankle) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Christie will be back following a one-game absence. However, his role has been minimal this season, so his return won’t impact the Clippers’ rotation.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Friday.
body: Williams will remain sidelined for a sixth straight game. Aday Mara has been starting recently and has taken on extra minutes with Williams unavailable, which is a trend that should continue against LA.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to play against the Clippers on Friday.
body: Mitchell missed Wednesday’s game against Portland, which allowed Alex Caruso to slide into the starting unit. Caruso contributed 14 points, three steals and four triples in the loss and would be worth streaming if Mitchell ends up missing another game.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mouhamed Gueye has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
body: The latest update has Gueye progressing in the right direction, with his next evaluation scheduled for some time around Dec. 10. Gueye will be a solid depth forward for Atlanta, but he’ll only make a fantasy impact if there is an injury to someone in front of him.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Joel Embiid will start against the Raptors on Thursday.
body: Wade will get the starting nod with LeBron James sidelined. This will likely be a singular start for Wade, though the 76ers do have a back-to-back coming up on Sunday and Monday, so Wade could be in line for another start.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Joel Embiid (foot) is available to play against the Raptors on Thursday.
body: Embiid will be good to go despite the initial questionable tag after seemingly tweaking his foot in Tuesday’s loss. He’ll occupy his usual spot in the starting unit.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Morez Johnson Jr. (shin) is available to play against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Johnson will be back following a one-game absence. That allowed Santi Aldama to take on a larger role off the bench. With Johnson back, both players will need minutes, which will likely limit the fantasy impact of both players.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Bryce McGowens (elbow) is doubtful to play against the Grizzlies on Friday.
body: McGowens has taken on extra minutes over the last two games, but he hasn’t been part of the Pelicans’ rotation for most of the year. His absence won’t open the door for anyone to step into legit minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kings insider James Ham reports that Maxime Raynaud (knee) is progressing but has no official timeline to return.
body: The backup big man has yet to make his season debut, but until he returns, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa should continue to pickup the slack in the frontcourt.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Bennedict Mathurin (thumb) is doubtful to play against the Grizzlies on Friday.
body: Mathurin is expected to miss a second straight game with this thumb injury. Jordan Poole played 21 minutes in Mathurin’s absence on Wednesday and should provide most of the offense off the bench once again in this one. He scored 14 points in their last game and has upside, but Poole isn’t a reliable option.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) and Yves Missi (knee) are doubtful for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: Murphy will miss a third straight game, and Missi will be sidelined for an 11th straight. With the pair expected to sit out against Memphis, Saddiq Bey and Karlo Matkovic should continue to handle additional playing time.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: LeBron James (sciatica) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the Raptors.
body: James will get a maintenance night for his back, and that could lead to more playing time for Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Miami Heat insider Ira Winderman reports that Klay Thompson (ankle) and Pelle Larsson (illness) missed Thursday’s practice.
body: According to Winderman, Thompson injured his ankle on a chase-down block in Tuesday’s matchup with the Jazz. If both Thompson and Larsson end up sitting out Friday’s matchup with the Cavaliers, more minutes could be available for Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Moussa Diabaté (quad) is available for Thursday’s matchup with the Suns.
body: Diabaté will return from a two-game absence, and he should reclaim his starting job. That should mean fewer minutes for Ryan Kalkbrenner and Hannes Steinbach.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Grant Williams (hamstring) will make his season debut Thursday against the Suns.
body: Given Charlotte’s multiple injuries, Williams may not have the luxury of being eased back into action. He’s not a guy to get into fantasy lineups right away, but managers in deeper leagues should keep an eye on his workload.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Trayce Jackson-Davis (illness) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the 76ers.
body: TJD will miss both legs of Toronto’s back-to-back set, though since he hasn’t played much this season, his availability won’t be majorly impactful for fantasy managers.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the 76ers.
body: Barnes will miss a fourth straight game while dealing with a left groin strain. That should mean another start for Collin Murray-Boyles, who has averaged 13.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.0 “stocks” across his last four starts.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Steph Curry sustained an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
body: Curry sustained the injury in Wednesday’s loss to Houston, and it will keep him out until late November at minimum. In Curry’s absence, De’Anthony Melton should handle an expanded role after logging 25 minutes Wednesday after Curry’s early exit. Will Richard could also see some additional playing time until Curry returns.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Aday Mara notched 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: For the first time in his young NBA career, Mara played over 30 minutes in a game. He logged 32 minutes against the Trail Blazers, but the final stat line wasn’t strong enough to make the rookie a must-start in all leagues. Mara replaced Kenrich Williams (11/2/2 with one block and two three-pointers) in the starting lineup, and who starts moving forward may be dictated by the opposition’s rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: A double-digit scorer in seven straight games, Holiday provided solid fantasy value on Wednesday. In addition to the 19 points, he shot 5-of-8 from beyond the arc and recorded good numbers in assists and steals. Through 11 games, Holiday has been close to a top-100 fantasy player, something most managers did not expect before the season began.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: While Lillard didn’t lead the way offensively for the Trail Blazers as he did in Wednesday’s win over Oklahoma City, the production remained solid. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of Portland’s first 11 games, and Dame has started every game. As long as he stays healthy, Lillard should be able to deliver a top-100 season, if not more.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.
body: Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski accounted for 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.
body: For the first time this season, Podziemski has scored at least 20 points in consecutive games. He finished with a solid stat line, missing only a blocked shot. And the Warriors may need even more from Podziemski in the short term, as Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic.
body: Over the past week, Darryn Peterson has gotten more confident, aggressive, and the Jazz have been letting him lose. The peripheral stats from college have started to come back, and it’s been exciting to watch. You want more in terms of efficiency, but with Lauri Markkanen out for a month, Darryn is a must roster if he hasn’t been picked up in your league already.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ace Bailey put up 18 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, four blocks, and three 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday.
body: Ace Bailey has been great this season and has been one of the best shot blockers in the NBA. His ability to havoc defender at this point is a great sign for his long-term development. He’s coachable and is a great teammate. The efficiency wasn’t great in this one, but it’s hard to complain with the peripheral stats that he gave you in this one.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Brice Senabaugh scored 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, a steal, a block, and three 3-pointers in loss to the Magic.
body: Brice Sensabaugh has had a rough month of November, but it was good to see a bounce back game from the scoring department. Sensabaugh kept the Jazz afloat in the fourth quarter on the offensive end when the Magic shut off the water on everyone else. He remains a stream guy for points and 3’s in redraft leagues, but not a high priority one.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Anthony Black put up 22 points (6-of-14 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in win against the Jazz on Wednesday.
body: Back-to-Back great games against the Kings and the Jazz. He was aggressive in looking for his shot and it helped lead them to the win. This season, he’s been awesome from a statistical perspective and hitting his 3’s. The Magic are going to need to make a decision to trade one of their core places if they want to keep him around.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Desmond Bane scored 25 points (9-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, a steal, and seven 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.
body: Desmond Bane’s 3PT shooting was a massive weapon to the Magic in this one and was a big reason why the Magic were able to pull away in the fourth quarter. You would want more in the peripheral stats, but this is about what you would expect from Desmond Bane on a night-to-night basis.

headline: Franz Wagner with a monster 38 points (13-of-23 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), eight rebounds, an assist, a steal, and three 3-pointers in a 123-108 win over the Jazz on Wednesday.
body: Franz Wagner led the way for the Magic in this one and he really helped spearhead this offense. These are the types of performances that you want as a Franz owner without Paolo. It’s easier when you’re going against the Jazz, but it’s good see him hit some 3’s in this one. He started talking smack to the Jazz and really got going in the fourth quarter.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Marcus Smart was ejected from Wednesday’s game against the Warriors with 21 seconds left in the third quarter.
body: Smart’s night ended prematurely after getting tangled up with Warriors center Charles Bassey late in the third quarter. The Rockets guard threw a punch that grazed Bassey’s nose. Smart finished with six points (2-of-2 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers. If he’s suspended, Reed Sheppard should get more minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome had 22 points (9-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, and a three in loss on Wednesday.
body: Jerome has had 5 straight games of at least 20 points which is awesome for fantasy owners. He led the team with a +9 in a five point loss. If you got Jerome at ADP, you got an absolute monster of a steal on draft day. Unless he gets traded, there’s no sign of this slowing down. He fits very well with this team and he’s really contributing to winning.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ryan Rollins (head) recorded eight points (3-of-10 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kel’el Ware produced eight points (3-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal and three blocks in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro (knee) accounted for 27 points (8-of-16 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylen Wells scored 22 points (6-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, an assist, and five 3-pointers in loss to the Nuggets on Wednesday.
body: Jaylen’s shot making is what kept Memphis in this game with his 3PT shooting. His game is pretty empty apart from the 3’s and the points, but he’s still a very valuable player as a threat as a shooter. His value as an NBA player is very stable with how the NBA wants these wings shooters that can play good defense.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 25 points (7-of-16 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: After starting each of Milwaukee’s first 11 games, Jaquez was moved to the bench on Wednesday. Given his productivity, that may be a role the Bucks ask Jaquez to take on moving forward. Recording his first 20-point game since October 24 against the 76ers, Jaquez finished with a season-high 25 as part of a solid overall stat line. He was runner-up for NBA Sixth Man of the Year last season, so this isn’t a foreign role for Jaquez. And it may raise his fantasy ceiling if the Bucks continue to bring him off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Sexton (head) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, three assists and one steal.
body: With Quentin Grimes (finger) unavailable for Wednesday’s game, Sexton’s role had added importance. Unfortunately, while he did hit double figures, the Lakers guard had to leave with just under seven minutes left in the fourth quarter. Sexton banged heads with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins, and both left the game and did not return. Sexton’s cut required sutures, but there were no reports that he might have to enter the league’s concussion protocol.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walker Kessler amassed 10 points (5-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
body: The Lakers have played seven games in November, and Kessler has recorded a double-double in six of them. In addition to the double-doubles, the 7-footer has blocked at least one shot in 11 of 13 games this season. Thus far, Kessler has been everything that fantasy managers hoped he would be in Los Angeles, and then some.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
body: Mamukelashvili was at his best during the second quarter, shooting 4-of-4 from the field and scoring 10 points. He didn’t provide much beyond points and three-pointers, but Mamu has been productive enough this season to merit a roster spot in deep leagues. Despite not playing the same position, Mamukelashvili would be worth streaming if either Luka Dončić (ankle) or Austin Reaves (heel) misses Friday’s game against the Spurs.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Nets.
body: Downgraded from probable to doubtful late Wednesday morning, Murphy will miss a second straight game. Saddiq Bey started Monday’s loss to the Warriors but offered little production. However, Wednesday’s matchup should be a better one for him.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles, and Jakob Poeltl on Wednesday against the Celtics
body: Immanuel Quickley will return to the starting lineup after returning from his hamstring injury which will send Jamal Shead back tot he bench. Shead is now more of a deeper league guy.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Derrick White, Baylor Scheierman, Jayson Tatum, Luka Garza and Neemias Queta will start Wednesday’s game against the Raptors.
body: The Celtics have made two changes to the lineup that began Tuesday’s win over the 76ers. Scheierman will replace Jordan Walsh, who is available but will come off the bench. The other change is Garza, who steps in for Paul George (rest).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) will be available to play against the Knicks on Wednesday.
body: Jaylon Tyson will return from his six game absence and be available for tonight’s game against the New York Knicks. He will likely be coming off the bench and providing some needed scoring. With him back, Tyrese Proctor will likely take a reduced role which will be important to note for deeper leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) will be available to play against the Celtics on Wednesday.
body: Jaylon Tyson will return from his six game absence and be available for tonight’s game against the Boston Celtics. He will likely be coming off the bench and providing some needed scoring. With him back, Tyrese Proctor will likely take a reduced role which will be important to note for deeper leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Andrew Nembhard, Kelly Oubre Jr., Aaron Nesmith, Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac will start Wednesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: After starting the Pacers’ last four games, rookie Braden Smith has been moved to the bench. Oubre will move into the starting lineup as the Pacers continue without the injured Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring).
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro (knee) is a game-time decision for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Injured during Sunday’s loss to the Celtics, Herro did not play in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. If he remains out, Ryan Rollins will remain in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell (back) will miss Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Coach Tiago Splitter also said that Norman Powell is at 70 percent, so there’s a chance he misses more than just tonight’s game. Isaac Okoro started in his spot last game, so it’s likely that Splitter goes to him again as a starter. Okoro could be worth a stream depending on your league but there’s not a lot of upside for a great game from a statistical perspective.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Devin Vassell (groin) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Bulls.
body: Initially questionable for Wednesday’s game, Vassell will miss a second straight as he continues to deal with a groin injury. Julian Champagnie should remain in the starting lineup until Vassell is cleared to return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Caleb Wilson (hip) is a game-time decision against the Lakers on Wednesday.
body: If Caleb Wilson were to miss time, look for Matas Buzelis to pick up more usage, with Noa Essengue or Patrick Williams picking up more of the minutes. However, none of them are major priorities to streaming priorities unless you’re in deeper leagues.

headline: Dailyn Swain (back) is now questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Initially absent from the injury report released by the Bulls on Tuesday, Swain is now questionable. That’s not a good sign regarding his availability for Wednesday’s game. However, Swain’s status won’t affect fantasy basketball, as he’s been out of the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: McConnell is available, but his playing time is likely to be limited. After playing eight minutes in his first appearance of the season on Saturday, the veteran point guard played nine minutes in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Kawhi Leonard (knee) is doing individual work and progressing well.
body: Leonard has not appeared in a game since October 23, and it was announced on Tuesday that he would be re-evaluated in one week. Rajakovic’s update is positive, but Leonard remains limited to individual work. When available, Collin Murray-Boyles has been part of the starting lineup in recent games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns (calf) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers.
body: Towns has yet to miss a game this season, and that won’t change on Wednesday. He’ll take on his usual starting role, with Andre Drummond remaining the backup center.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Egor Dëmin (leg) is available to play against the Pelicans on Wednesday.
body: Following a six-game absence, Dëmin will be back in the mix for Brooklyn. His return will help offset the second straight absence for Mikel Brown Jr. (illness), and with Nolan Traoré (calf) questionable, Dëmin could see a bump in usage.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trayce Jackson-Davis (illness) has been ruled out against the Celtics on Wednesday.
body: Jackson-Davis has only played a small role off the bench this season, so his absence won’t drastically alter Toronto’s rotation.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Mikel Brown Jr. (illness) has been ruled out against the Pelicans on Wednesday.
body: Brown missed Sunday’s game against Dallas with a back injury but wasn’t initially on this injury report. However, an illness will keep him sidelined for a second straight game. Keon Ellis should take on extra minutes off the bench with Brown unavailable.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Bennedict Mathurin (thumb) has been ruled out against the Nets on Wednesday.
body: Mathurin played a season-high 24 minutes in Monday’s blowout loss to the Warriors, but he had played less than 10 minutes in the previous two games. Bryce McGowens may see a few extra minutes with Mathurin unavailable.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) is now doubtful to play against the Nets on Wednesday.
body: Murphy was initially listed as probable for this game after missing Monday’s game, but he is now expected to be sidelined for at least one more game. Saddiq Bey started in place of Murphy on Monday and should get the nod once again.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ajay Mitchell recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jared McCain tallied 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: After scoring 19 points off the bench in Saturday’s rout of the Wizards, McCain returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Tuesday. Shooting 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, the third-year guard recorded his third 20-point stat line of the season. While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
body: Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. The final three points came on a 35-footer as time expired, giving Portland a 17-point lead heading into the fourth quarter. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Chris Youngblood (foot) will not return to Tuesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Youngblood injured his right foot early in the fourth quarter and has been ruled out for the rest of the night. Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson can absorb the minutes that would have gone to Youngblood, who is sitting on the Trail Blazers’ bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Precious Achiuwa (leg) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Magic with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench. Keegan Murray (11/2/1 with four blocks and two three-pointers) played 24 minutes as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine recorded 31 points (10-of-16 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic.
body: While fellow Kings veteran Domantas Sabonis went scoreless on Tuesday, LaVine had one of his most productive games of the season. He recorded his second 30-point game of the season, but he had to head to the locker room during the third quarter with an apparent ankle injury. Sacramento doesn’t play again until Friday, so LaVine will have a little time to recover.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr. amassed 29 points (10-of-21 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Magic.
body: Acuff continues to impress for the Kings, who fell to 1-10 on Tuesday. The rookie guard has scored at least 20 points in nine of Sacramento’s 11 games, and he’s been a first-round player in 12-team leagues over the last two weeks. As long as he keeps the turnovers in check, Acuff will be a highly valuable fantasy option, regardless of league format.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nate Ament recorded 10 points (4-of-8 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: For the second time in as many games, Ament surpassed 20 minutes, playing 22 against the Knicks. The rookie’s stat line only lacked a blocked shot, and he shot 50 percent from the field. Unlike fellow Bucks rookie Brayden Burries (three points, three rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer), Ament’s chances to provide consistent fantasy value early in the season are unlikely to be there. That said, he’s someone who could be valuable to fantasy managers after the February trade deadline.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Rollins amassed 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: The Bucks didn’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, so Rollins made his first start since Halloween. While the production was solid, he logged 24 minutes, with Kasparas Jakučionis (11 points, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers) playing 23 minutes off the bench. If Herro remains out for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers, Rollins may still have some value in 12-team leagues. That said, his recent move to the bench and reduced minutes are a major concern for managers who selected Rollins with a middle-round pick.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaime Jaquez Jr. finished Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks with 16 points (6-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: With Tyler Herro out with an injury, Jaquez led the Bucks starters in shot attempts and points Tuesday. Unfortunately, his efficiency suffered, especially in turnovers. Jaquez recorded a team-high four turnovers, the most he’s had in a game since racking up six in an October 23 loss to the Bulls. The good news is that Jaquez won’t have long to dwell on this performance, as the Bucks host the Lakers on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Black, Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner, Jamal Cain and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Tuesday’s game against the Kings.
body: The Magic have made two changes to their starting lineup. Bane is back after missing Saturday’s loss to the Warriors, and Tristan da Silva (calf) being out opened up a spot for Orlando’s usual starting off-guard. The other change is Cain, whose insertion into the starting lineup comes at Jase Richardson’s expense.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, De’Andre Hunter, Precious Achiuwa and Domantas Sabonis will start Tuesday’s game against the Magic.
body: Sabonis is back after missing Sunday’s loss to the Heat and will start. His return pushes Dylan Cardwell to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darryn Peterson, Josh Okogie, Josh Green, Ace Bailey and Jaxson Hayes will start Tuesday’s game against the Heat.
body: With Keyonte George (ankle) sidelined, the Jazz are shifting Peterson into the starting point guard role. That should raise his ceiling considerably. Replacing George in the starting lineup is Okogie, who will be more valuable to the Jazz than to fantasy managers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (wrist) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Not long after his status was downgraded from probable to questionable, the Heat said that Antetokounmpo will play on Tuesday. He’ll take on his usual role as the focal point of the Heat offense.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cam Christie (ankle) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Initially questionable for Tuesday’s game, Christie’s absence will not significantly impact fantasy basketball or the Clippers’ rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White, Paul George, Jordan Walsh, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta will start Tuesday’s game against the 76ers.
body: After starting Mike Conley in Sunday’s win over the Bucks, the Celtics are calling on Jordan Walsh to start. While limited as a scorer, his defense will be key against Philadelphia’s offensive firepower.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo (wrist) has been downgraded to questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Antetokounmpo’s status is trending in the wrong direction after the Heat listed him as probable on the initial injury report. If he can’t play, the Heat may rely more on Nikola Jović at power forward.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Rollins, Brayden Burries, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner will start Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: The Bucks won’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, as he’s out with a leg injury. Rollins returns to the starting lineup for the first time since Halloween, which raises his short-term fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zion Williamson (rest) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Nets.
body: Williamson did not play in Monday’s loss to the Warriors, with Saddiq Bey replacing him in the starting lineup. Zion’s return means that Bey will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kel’el Ware (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Added to the Bucks’ injury report Tuesday afternoon, Ware is good to go. He’ll take on his usual backup center role, which limits the 7-footer’s fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tyler Herro (leg) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Herro injured his leg during Sunday’s loss to the Celtics and will not play on Tuesday. Herro’s absence could mean Ryan Rollins returns to the starting lineup, raising his fantasy ceiling.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Quentin Grimes (finger) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Grimes injured a finger on his right hand during Sunday’s win over the Pistons and did not play the following night against the Hawks. If he can play on Wednesday, Grimes will return to his usual reserve role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves (illness) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Reaves did not play in Monday’s win over the Hawks. With Quentin Grimes also out, Ziaire Williams returned to the starting lineup. Either Williams or Jake LaRavia is likely to come off the bench on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Stewart has missed the Grizzlies’ last two games, most recently sitting out Monday’s win over the Raptors. With Quinten Post (concussion) unavailable, Taylor Hendricks could move into the rotation if Beef Stew remains out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto reports that the Lakers signed Carson Cooper to a two-way contract.
body: Not selected in the 2026 draft, Cooper began the season on a two-way deal with the Grizzlies and appeared in one game. He’ll join the Lakers on a similar deal, and Lawson Lovering has been waived to open up a two-way slot for Cooper.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Hart (illness) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Downgraded from questionable to doubtful due to an illness, Hart will miss a third straight game. Landry Shamet will start until Hart, who is also recovering from an ankle injury, is cleared to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nolan Traoré (calf) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Traoré is dealing with a sore right calf and could miss a game for the first time this season. Egor Dëmin is on track to return from a leg injury, so he could be first in line to run the point if Traoré can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Egor Dëmin (leg) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Dëmin is on track to play after missing Brooklyn’s last six games with a right leg injury. With Nolan Traoré (calf) questionable, the Nets may have to rely on Dëmin more as a playmaker if he can play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tobe Awaka (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Awaka did not play in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers and has not gotten the minutes needed to impact fantasy basketball when available. He should be rostered only in deep dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Dailyn Swain (back) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Swain is available after missing Sunday’s loss to the 76ers. The rookie should be rostered only in dynasty leagues, as he hasn’t played consistent rotation minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach Collins (illness) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Due to a respiratory illness, Collins did not play in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers. His availability does not impact fantasy basketball, especially with Nic Claxton back from a strained hamstring.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Powell did not play in Sunday’s loss to the 76ers, with a shoulder injury being the reason. The veteran guard is now dealing with lower back spasms. If Powell remains out, Isaac Okoro should get another start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Will Richard (thumb) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Rockets.
body: Richard, who suffered a torn UCL in his left thumb, did not play in Monday’s win over the Pelicans. LJ Cryer, whose minutes were also boosted by Brandon Williams’ hamstring injury, played 20 minutes off the bench. With the Warriors winning that game by 51 points, it’s unlikely Cryer plays that much if Richard remains out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Gary Payton II (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Rockets.
body: While Payton’s continued absence frees up additional minutes for De’Anthony Melton, it does not impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Murray-Boyles did not play in Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies, leading to Kyle Anderson’s first start of the season. Anderson played only 16 minutes and isn’t worth streaming if CMB remains out.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Trayce Jackson-Davis (illness) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Jackson-Davis’s availability doesn’t affect fantasy basketball, even if Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) misses another game.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Wizards.
body: After playing nine minutes in his first appearance of the season on Saturday, McConnell played eight minutes in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks. Even if he’s available on Wednesday, the veteran point guard is unlikely to get the minutes he needs to impact fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sam Merrill (elbow) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Merrill has missed Cleveland’s last two games due to management of a right elbow injury. Meleek Thomas has seen his opportunities increase, and that may remain the case on Wednesday if Merrill can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kawhi Leonard (knee) will miss at least one more week.
body: Leonard is continuing the reconditioning process after receiving treatment to address swelling in his left knee, according to the Raptors. They’ll provide another update on Leonard a week from now. Ja’Kobe Walter will continue to start in his absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Kel’el Ware (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Ware popped up on the injury report Tuesday afternoon as questionable with a left ankle sprain. Potentially on the wrong side of questionable, some of Ware’s backup center minutes could go to Nate Ament if he’s ruled out.
author: Nick Shlain
